html:
The Shanenawa are a small Panoan people of Acre in western Brazil, living on the Envira River near the town of Feijó.

Like their Huni Kuin and Yaminawa neighbours, they were drawn into debt labour on rubber estates during the Amazon rubber boom, which brought epidemics and broke up their villages. Their language is nearly gone: in 2016 only about two dozen people spoke it. Little else is recorded of their history.
sum: The Shanenawa are a small Panoan people of Acre in western Brazil, living on the Envira River near the town of Feijó.
